what_happened: Scene: layout 9 (same kitchen as s0), pan_8 (dark pan, long dark-brown handle with a hanging hole at its end) in a high upper cabinet; the 5-burner gas hob with the fish on a cutting board is ~2.3 m to the right; target front_center. Stage 0: the gripper went to the very END of the handle (the hole is between/above the fingers, 112-120) and closed at 121 with width 0.037 (pinching only the tip). 130-178 it pulled the pan out of the cabinet by the handle tip (hold 130-179); the pan tilted and at ~178-180 slipped out (fingers closed to 0.003 at 184). The pan fell 0.50 m onto the counter next to the toaster and landed upside-down (tipped from 182, tilt 180 deg to the end). The policy did not go back for it: it turned to the hob (250-400), picked the fish at 885 (lift 0.14 m), carried it over the bare hob and let it fall on the cooktop at ~960 (no pan there). It then worked the knobs: front_center (the task knob) to 0.93 rad at ~1103-1145, back to 0, then 0.35 from ~1509 to the end; front_right to 0.64 (~2200) and rear_right to 0.48/0.32 (~2400-2900). Flames are visible from ~1540. Stage 0/1/2 never held because the pan was on the counter 2.27 m away.
causal_chain: pinched the pan by the handle tip (121, width 0.037) -> pan pulled out and slipped out of the fingers at ~180 -> fell 0.5 m to the counter upside-down -> policy continued as if the pan were placed: fish dropped on the bare cooktop (960), three knobs turned (1080-2700) -> pan never on the burner -> timeout
self_recovery: none for the pan; it never looked back at it. It executed stages 1-2 motions on an empty hob.
official_criterion_notes: stage2:stove done_intervals [[1103,1145],[1509,2900]] = task knob front_center >= 0.35 (end 0.353, barely), while pan and fish are not in place; stage 2 correctly never holds.

fish hold 894-960 lift 0.139, end on cooktop 2.37 m from target
